findings.text: The dispatch door never hands its reservation to the supervisor it starts: _start_supervisor(spec_path, directory, run_id) is called with no reservation keyword, while dispatch_launch.py:2982 and :2992 are the only sites that call record_reservation_supervisor. The reservation therefore keeps naming the dispatching process, so reservation_in_flight falls to its process arm for the whole life of that process. On the admit door, which calls dispatch in-process from a long-lived loop (queue_admission.py:441), the reservation is held until the service restarts, so a run relaunched once is refused forever after its worker has ended, against the deliverable's 'no launch that has ended, or been killed, leaves the run unlaunchable'. Off the fleet the same omission frees the hold the moment the dispatch CLI exits, which reopens the very window between attempt.json and worker.json that the node exists to close. Repair is passing reservation=reservation at this call.

No assertion covers the path that is defective: test_a_recorded_supervisor_that_exited_frees_the_reservation builds the reservation with _reservation(... supervisor_pid=_dead_pid()) and never runs a launch, so it holds whether or not any door records a supervisor. The plan's admit-door case, 'a run launched through the admit door, whose admitting process stays alive, becomes launchable again once its recorded supervisor has exited', has no case that drives dispatch to completion and then reads the reservation it left behind. A case asserting that the reservation file remaining after a dispatch names the supervisor pid would redden on the reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3488 defect.

The plan requires 'the same race for a run that is not its node's newest committed run still yields one reservation and one refusal', and no case represents it: test_a_resume_and_a_dispatch_take_the_same_key reserves twice on one run directory with no ledger at all. The hazard is structurally absent today because launch_reservation_key reads only the run's own receipts, so the missing case cannot expose a live defect, but nothing would redden if a door began keying on prior_node_runs[-1] again.

Four hunks of this file are reflowed lines the change does not otherwise touch (the sorts at :475 and :617, the refusal string at :570, the identity expression at :969). The node's own rubric claims only declared modules were written, which is true, but the reformatting enlarges the review surface and belongs in its own sweep per the repository's lint policy.

claim_next_attempt, release_attempt_claim and _claim_may_be_reclaimed now have no production caller after _resume switched to the reservation; only tests/test_a_resume_never_launches_beside_another_node.py exercises them. The plan ruled the claim out for reuse, which is why a second primitive was written, but leaving the retired one in place means the module still presents two attempt-claiming mechanisms with different keys and different release rules. Retiring it is fenced out of this node's scope because that test file is not in its write paths, so this is recorded for a follow-up rather than repaired here.

_set_reservation_aside renames an abandoned reservation to attempt-N.reservation.reclaimed.<pid> inside the run directory and nothing ever removes it, so every reclaim leaves a file in a directory whose listing run_holds_an_attempt_record and the receipt readers walk. The names do not match _ATTEMPT_RECEIPT_PATTERN or _RESERVATION_PATTERN, so correctness is unaffected; the cost is unbounded accumulation in the run record of a run that is relaunched repeatedly.

justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path in d36e465b39, d47523edc2 and 34d0376761 is inside the six declared write paths, though reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:969 carries a reformat of lines the change does not otherwise touch.
